You are jolly_ember22, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Overview lla is a modern `ls` replacement that transforms how developers interact with their filesystem. Built with Rust's performance capabilities and designed with user experience in mind, lla combines the familiarity of `ls` with powerful features like specialized views, Git integration, and a robust plugin system with an extensible list of plugins to add more functionality. ## Features - Multiple Views: Default clean view, long format, tree structure, table layout, grid display - Diff Command: Human-friendly directory or file comparisons (local ↔ local or git) with size/line deltas and unified diff output - Git Integration: Built-in status visualization and repository insights - Advanced Organization: Timeline view, storage analysis, recursive exploration - Smart Navigation: Interactive directory jumper with bookmarks and history - Smart Search: complex filtering patterns (OR, AND, NOT, XOR), regex support, content search - Customization: Plugin system, theme manager, custom shortcuts, configurable display - High Performance: Built with Rust, modern UI, clean listings - Smart Sorting: Multiple criteria, directory-first option, natural sorting - Flexible Config: Easy initialization, plugin management, configuration tools - Rich Plugin Ecosystem: File ops and metadata enhancements, code analysis, git tools, and more - Smart Filters: Range-based size/time filters, reusable presets, cache-aware refinements - Git-aware Filtering: Optional `.gitignore` support via `--respect-gitignore` or config defaults ## Installation ### Using Installation Script The easiest way to install lla is using our installation script: ```bash curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chaqchase/lla/main/install.sh | bash ``` This script will automatically: - Detect your OS and architecture - Download the appropriate binary - Verify the checksum - Install lla to `/usr/local/bin` ### Using Package Manager | Package Manager / Platform | Command | | -------------------------- | ------------------- | | Cargo | `cargo install lla` | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install lla` | | Arch Linux (paru) | `paru -S lla` | | NetBSD (pkgin) | `pkgin install lla` | | X-CMD | `x install lla` | ### Manual Installation ```bash # Manual - Example is for amd64 GNU, replaces the file names if downloading for a different arch. wget -c https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/releases/download//-> -O lla # Example /v0.3.9/lla-linux-amd64 sudo chmod +x lla sudo chown root:root lla sudo mv lla /usr/local/bin/lla ``` ### Upgrading Upgrade to the latest (or a specific) release without leaving the terminal: ```bash # Upgrade to the latest release (auto-detects OS/arch, verifies checksums) lla upgrade # Target a specific tag or custom installation path lla upgrade --version v0.5.1 --path /usr/local/bin/lla ``` The upgrade command reuses the official install script logic, renders animated progress indicators, verifies the `SHA256SUMS` manifest, and atomically swaps the `lla` binary in place (defaults to the path of the running executable—override with `--path` if needed). ### Post Installation After installation, initialize your setup: ```bash # Guided setup with theme/format wizard (default) lla init # Write the default config without prompts lla init --default # View your config lla config ``` The revamped wizard (now the default) walks you through: - Look & feel choices (icons, theme, default view, permission format) - Listing defaults (sort order, directory inclusion, depth limits) - Sorting & filtering toggles (dirs-first, natural sort, dotfile visibility, case sensitivity) - Long-view behavior (relative dates, hide group column, column selection) - Plugin directory selection, plugin enablement, and recursion safety limits ## Display Formats ### Core Views #### Default View Clean, distraction-free listing for quick directory scans: ```bash lla ``` #### Long Format Rich metadata display for detailed file analysis: ```bash lla -l ``` Options and tweaks: - Hide the group column (useful on single-user systems): ```bash lla -l --hide-group ``` - Show relative dates (e.g., "2h ago"): ```bash lla -l --relative-dates ``` To make these defaults, add to your config (`~/.config/lla/config.toml`): ```toml [formatters.long] hide_group = true relative_dates = true columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "user", "group", "name", "field:git_status", "field:tags"] ``` The `columns` array lets you control the precise column order. Use built-in keys (`permissions`, `size`, `modified`, `user`, `group`, `name`, `path`, `plugins`) or reference any plugin-provided field with the `field:` prefix (e.g., `field:git_status`, `field:complexity_score`). #### Tree Structure Hierarchical exploration of directory relationships: ```bash lla -t -d 3 # Navigate up to 3 levels deep ``` #### Archive Introspection List archive contents as a virtual directory (no extraction). Supported: `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`. ``` lla my_archive.zip -t # tree view lla project.tar.gz -l # long view lla my_archive.tgz --json lla my_archive.zip -l -f ".rs" # filter by extension on internal paths ``` #### Single-file Listing You can pass a single file path to list it directly with any view or machine output: ``` lla README.md # default view lla Cargo.toml -l # long view lla src/main.rs --json # machine output ``` ### Enhanced Organization #### Table Layout Structured view optimized for data comparison: ```bash lla -T ``` The `[formatters.table].columns` setting mirrors the long-view syntax, so you can mix built-in fields with plugin-provided metadata: ```toml [formatters.table] columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "name", "field:git_branch", "field:git_commit"] ``` #### Diff View (Files & Directories) Compare directories or individual files (including against git references) with compact, colorized summaries. Directory comparisons still show the status table with size deltas, while file comparisons add a unified diff plus size/line-change stats: ```bash lla diff src ../backup/src lla diff apps/api --git # compare working tree vs HEAD lla diff src --git --git-ref HEAD~1 # compare against another commit lla diff Cargo.lock ../backup/Cargo.lock lla diff Cargo.lock --git --git-ref HEAD~1 ``` For directories, the diff view groups entries by status, colors the change indicator, and shows left/right sizes plus the net delta so you can spot growth at a glance. For files, lla prints a size summary, line-count delta, and a git-style unified diff (with automatic binary detection so unreadable data isn’t dumped to your terminal). #### Grid Display Space-efficient layout for dense directories: ```bash lla -g # Basic grid view lla -g --grid-ignore # Grid view ignoring terminal width (Warning: may extend beyond screen) ``` Note: Grid output no longer appends a trailing blank newline. ### Specialized Views #### Git Integration Smart repository insights: ```bash lla -G ``` #### Timeline Organization Chronological file tracking: ```bash lla --timeline ``` #### Storage Analysis Visual disk usage insights, including a total size summary: ```bash lla -S # use --include-dirs to calculate directory sizes (recursive; slower on large trees) ``` ### Advanced Navigation #### Jump-to-Directory (Interactive Directory Jumper) Quickly navigate to bookmarked or recently visited directories with an interactive keyboard-driven prompt: ```bash # One-time setup for seamless directory jumping lla jump --setup # Interactive directory selection lla jump # Add directory to bookmarks lla jump --add ~/projects/my-app # Remove bookmark lla jump --remove ~/projects/my-app # List all bookmarks and recent history lla jump --list # Clear history lla jump --clear-history ``` **Features:** - **Interactive Selection**: Arrow keys and Enter to select from bookmarked and recent directories - **Smart History**: Automatically records directory visits (respects `exclude_paths`) - **Bookmarks**: Add favorite directories for quick access - **Deduplication**: No duplicate entries in history - **Shell Integration**: Works seamlessly with shell commands like `cd` **How it works:** 1. Built with Rust's performance capabilities and designed with user experience in mind, lla combines the familiarity of `ls` with powerful features like specialized views, Git integration, and a robust plugin system with an extensible list of plugins to add more functionality. ![default](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba5fa273-c2c4-4143-b199-ab5bff1bb608) ## Features - Smart Search: complex filtering patterns (OR, AND, NOT, XOR), regex support - Customization: Plugin system, theme manager, custom shortcuts, configurable display - High Performance: Built with Rust, modern UI, clean listings - Smart Sorting: Multiple criteria, directory-first option, natural sorting - Flexible Config: Easy initialization, plugin management, configuration tools - Rich Plugin Ecosystem: File ops and metadata enhancements, code analysis, git tools, and more ## Installation ```bash # Using Cargo cargo install lla ``` For more installation options, documentation, and detailed usage instructions, visit: [lla Github repository](https://github.com/chaqchase/lla) # lla Plugins This is a list of all the plugins available for lla. ## Installation You can install all prebuilt plugins at once using the default installer: ```bash lla install ``` To force fetching the latest prebuilt archive (useful after a release): ```bash # install pre-built plugins lla install --prebuilt # or install from a repo lla install --git https://github.com/chaqchase/lla ``` If you prefer to build from source, install them like this: ```bash git clone https://github.com/chaqchase/lla cd lla/plugins/ cargo build --release ``` then copy the generated `.so`, `.dll`, or `.dylib` file from the `target/release` directory to your lla plugins directory. ## Available Plugins - [categorizer](https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/tree/main/plugins/categorizer): Categorizes files based on their extensions and metadata - [code_complexity](https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/tree/main/plugins/code_complexity): Analyzes code complexity using various metrics - [code_snippet_extractor](https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/tree/main/plugins/code_snippet_extractor): A plugin for extracting and managing code snippets - [dirs_meta](https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/tree/main/plugins/dirs_meta): Shows directories metadata - [duplicate_file_detector](https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/tree/main/plugins/duplicate_file_detector): A plugin for the lla that detects duplicate files. - [file_hash](https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/tree/main/plugins/file_hash): Displays the hash of each file - lla

Modern, customizable, feature-rich and extensible `ls` replacement.
Documentation · Features · Installation · Display Formats · Command Reference

## Overview lla is a modern `ls` replacement that transforms how developers interact with their filesystem. Built with Rust's performance capabilities and designed with user experience in mind, lla combines the familiarity of `ls` with powerful features like specialized views, Git integration, and a robust plugin system with an extensible list of plugins to add more functionality. ## Features - Multiple Views: Default clean view, long format, tree structure, table layout, grid display - Diff Command: Human-friendly directory or file comparisons (local ↔ local or git) with size/line deltas and unified diff output - Git Integration: Built-in status visualization and repository insights - Advanced Organization: Timeline view, storage analysis, recursive exploration - Smart Navigation: Interactive directory jumper with bookmarks and history - Smart Search: complex filtering patterns (OR, AND, NOT, XOR), regex support, content search - Customization: Plugin system, theme manager, custom shortcuts, configurable display - High Performance: Built with Rust, modern UI, clean listings - Smart Sorting: Multiple criteria, directory-first option, natural sorting - Flexible Config: Easy initialization, plugin management, configuration tools - Rich Plugin Ecosystem: File ops and metadata enhancements, code analysis, git tools, and more - Smart Filters: Range-based size/time filters, reusable presets, cache-aware refinements - Git-aware Filtering: Optional `.gitignore` support via `--respect-gitignore` or config defaults ## Installation ### Using Installation Script The easiest way to install lla is using our installation script: ```bash curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chaqchase/lla/main/install.sh | bash ``` This script will automatically: - Detect your OS and architecture - Download the appropriate binary - Verify the checksum - Install lla to `/usr/local/bin` ### Using Package Manager | Package Manager / Platform | Command | | -------------------------- | ------------------- | | Cargo | `cargo install lla` | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install lla` | | Arch Linux (paru) | `paru -S lla` | | NetBSD (pkgin) | `pkgin install lla` | | X-CMD | `x install lla` | ### Manual Installation ```bash # Manual - Example is for amd64 GNU, replaces the file names if downloading for a different arch. wget -c https://github.com/chaqchase/lla/releases/download//-> -O lla # Example /v0.3.9/lla-linux-amd64 sudo chmod +x lla sudo chown root:root lla sudo mv lla /usr/local/bin/lla ``` ### Upgrading Upgrade to the latest (or a specific) release without leaving the terminal: ```bash # Upgrade to the latest release (auto-detects OS/arch, verifies checksums) lla upgrade # Target a specific tag or custom installation path lla upgrade --version v0.5.1 --path /usr/local/bin/lla ``` The upgrade command reuses the official install script logic, renders animated progress indicators, verifies the `SHA256SUMS` manifest, and atomically swaps the `lla` binary in place (defaults to the path of the running executable—override with `--path` if needed). ### Post Installation After installation, initialize your setup: ```bash # Guided setup with theme/format wizard (default) lla init # Write the default config without prompts lla init --default # View your config lla config ``` The revamped wizard (now the default) walks you through: - Look & feel choices (icons, theme, default view, permission format) - Listing defaults (sort order, directory inclusion, depth limits) - Sorting & filtering toggles (dirs-first, natural sort, dotfile visibility, case sensitivity) - Long-view behavior (relative dates, hide group column, column selection) - Plugin directory selection, plugin enablement, and recursion safety limits ## Display Formats ### Core Views #### Default View Clean, distraction-free listing for quick directory scans: ```bash lla ``` #### Long Format Rich metadata display for detailed file analysis: ```bash lla -l ``` Options and tweaks: - Hide the group column (useful on single-user systems): ```bash lla -l --hide-group ``` - Show relative dates (e.g., "2h ago"): ```bash lla -l --relative-dates ``` To make these defaults, add to your config (`~/.config/lla/config.toml`): ```toml [formatters.long] hide_group = true relative_dates = true columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "user", "group", "name", "field:git_status", "field:tags"] ``` The `columns` array lets you control the precise column order. Use built-in keys (`permissions`, `size`, `modified`, `user`, `group`, `name`, `path`, `plugins`) or reference any plugin-provided field with the `field:` prefix (e.g., `field:git_status`, `field:complexity_score`). #### Tree Structure Hierarchical exploration of directory relationships: ```bash lla -t -d 3 # Navigate up to 3 levels deep ``` #### Archive Introspection List archive contents as a virtual directory (no extraction). Supported: `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`. ``` lla my_archive.zip -t # tree view lla project.tar.gz -l # long view lla my_archive.tgz --json lla my_archive.zip -l -f ".rs" # filter by extension on internal paths ``` #### Single-file Listing You can pass a single file path to list it directly with any view or machine output: ``` lla README.md # default view lla Cargo.toml -l # long view lla src/main.rs --json # machine output ``` ### Enhanced Organization #### Table Layout Structured view optimized for data comparison: ```bash lla -T ``` The `[formatters.table].columns` setting mirrors the long-view syntax, so you can mix built-in fields with plugin-provided metadata: ```toml [formatters.table] columns = ["permissions", "size", "modified", "name", "field:git_branch", "field:git_commit"] ``` #### Diff View (Files & Directories) Compare directories or individual files (including against git references) with compact, colorized summaries. Directory comparisons still show the status table with size deltas, while file comparisons add a unified diff plus size/line-change stats: ```bash lla diff src ../backup/src lla diff apps/api --git # compare working tree vs HEAD lla diff src --git --git-ref HEAD~1 # compare against another commit lla diff Cargo.lock ../backup/Cargo.lock lla diff Cargo.lock --git --git-ref HEAD~1 ``` For directories, the diff view groups entries by status, colors the change indicator, and shows left/right sizes plus the net delta so you can spot growth at a glance. For files, lla prints a size summary, line-count delta, and a git-style unified diff (with automatic binary detection so unreadable data isn’t dumped to your terminal). #### Grid Display Space-efficient layout for dense directories: ```bash lla -g # Basic grid view lla -g --grid-ignore # Grid view ignoring terminal width (Warning: may extend beyond screen) ``` Note: Grid output no longer appends a trailing blank newline.

"""Plugin related CLI commands for lla."""
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path


LIST_HELP = """executable-list-plugins 
List all available plugins

USAGE:
    executable list-plugins

OPTIONS:
    -h, --help    Print help information
"""

PLUGIN_HELP = """executable-plugin 
Run a plugin action

USAGE:
    executable plugin [OPTIONS] [--] [ARGS]

ARGS:
    <plugin_name>       Name of the plugin
    <plugin_action>     Action to perform
    <plugin_args>...    Arguments for the plugin action

OPTIONS:
    -a, --action <action>    Action to perform (alternative to positional)
    -h, --help               Print help information
    -n, --name <name>        Name of the plugin (alternative to positional)
    -r, --args <args>...     Arguments for the plugin action (alternative to positional)
"""


def _plugin_dir():
    # Match the documented default; installed plugins are shared objects.
    cfg = Path.home() / ".config/lla/config.toml"
    try:
        import re
        txt = cfg.read_text()
        m = re.search(r'(?m)^plugins_dir\s*=\s*["\']([^"\']+)', txt)
        if m:
            return Path(os.path.expanduser(m.group(1)))
    except OSError:
        pass
    return Path.home() / ".config/lla/plugins"


def run(args):
    """Dispatch plugin subcommands; return True if consumed."""
    if not args or args[0] not in ("plugin", "list-plugins"):
        return False
    cmd, rest = args[0], args[1:]
    if cmd == "list-plugins":
        if any(a in ("-h", "--help") for a in rest):
            print(LIST_HELP)
        else:
            found = []
            try:
                for p in _plugin_dir().iterdir():
                    if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in (".so", ".dll", ".dylib"):
                        found.append(p.stem)
            except OSError:
                pass
            if not found:
                print("╭─ Plugins ───────────────────────────────────╮")
                print("│   ℹ  No plugins installed.                  │")
                print("│                                             │")
                print("│      Run lla install --help to get started. │")
                print("╰─────────────────────────────────────────────╯")
            else:
                print("╭─ Plugins ───────────────────────────────────╮")
                for name in sorted(found):
                    print(f"│   {name}")
                print("╰─────────────────────────────────────────────╯")
        return True

    if any(a in ("-h", "--help") for a in rest):
        print(PLUGIN_HELP)
        return True
    name = None
    positional = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(rest):
        if rest[i] in ("-n", "--name") and i + 1 < len(rest):
            name = rest[i + 1]; i += 2
        elif rest[i] in ("-a", "--action") and i + 1 < len(rest):
            positional.extend((name or "", rest[i + 1])); i += 2
        elif rest[i] in ("-r", "--args"):
            positional.extend(rest[i+1:]); break
        elif rest[i] == "--":
            positional.extend(rest[i+1:]); break
        elif not rest[i].startswith("-"):
            positional.append(rest[i]); i += 1
        else:
            i += 1
    if name:
        positional.insert(0, name)
    plugin = positional[0] if positional else ""
    print("\n✗ Plugin Error\n\n  Plugin '%s' not found.\n  \n  No plugins are currently installed. Run 'lla install' to install plugins.\n" % plugin)
    return True

+"""Local behavior for plugin install/update and CLI upgrade commands."""
+from pathlib import Path
+
+INSTALL_HELP = """executable-install 
+Install a plugin
+
+USAGE:
+    executable install [OPTIONS]
+
+OPTIONS:
+        --dir <dir>    Install a plugin from a local directory
+        --git <git>    Install a plugin from a GitHub repository URL
+    -h, --help         Print help information
+        --prebuilt     Install plugins from the latest prebuilt release (default)
+"""
+UPDATE_HELP = """executable-update
+Update installed plugins
+
+USAGE:
+    executable update [name]
+
+ARGS:
+    <name>    Name of the plugin to update (updates all if not specified)
+
+OPTIONS:
+    -h, --help    Print help information
+"""
+UPGRADE_HELP = """executable-upgrade
+Upgrade the lla CLI to the latest (or specified) release
+
+USAGE:
+    executable upgrade [OPTIONS]
+
+OPTIONS:
+    -h, --help                 Print help information
+        --path <path>          Install location for the lla binary (defaults to the current
+                               executable path)
+    -v, --version <version>    Upgrade to a specific release tag (defaults to the latest release)
+"""
+
+
+def run(argv):
+    """Handle commands whose normal successful path requires network access."""
+    if not argv or argv[0] not in ("install", "update", "upgrade"):
+        return False
+    cmd, args = argv[0], argv[1:]
+    if "--help" in args or "-h" in args:
+        print({"install": INSTALL_HELP, "update": UPDATE_HELP, "upgrade": UPGRADE_HELP}[cmd])
+        return True
+    if cmd == "update":
+        print("\n✗ Plugin Error\n\n  No plugins are currently installed\n")
+    elif cmd == "install":
+        if "--dir" in args:
+            i = args.index("--dir")
+            value = args[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(args) else ""
+            if not Path(value).is_dir():
+                print("╭─ lla ────────────────╮\n│   Local Installation │\n╰──────────────────────╯\n\n╭─ Source ──────────────────╮\n│   Directory  │  %s │\n╰───────────────────────────╯\n\n\n✗ Plugin Error\n\n  Directory not found: %s\n" % (value, value))

+        else:
+            print("\n✗ Plugin Error\n\n  Network access is unavailable\n")
+    else:
+        print("\n✗ Upgrade Error\n\n  Network access is unavailable\n")
+    return True
*** End Patch";

    a=parse_args(); root=os.path.abspath(a.directory)
    if not os.path.exists(root): print(f"\n✗ Error\n\n  Path '{a.directory}' does not exist or is not accessible\n",file=sys.stderr); return 1
    paths=[]
    if os.path.isfile(root) or os.path.islink(root): paths=[a.directory]
    else:
      def walk(d,level):
        try: entries=sorted(os.scandir(d),key=lambda e:e.name.casefold())
        except OSError: return
        for e in entries:
          if e.name in ('.','..'): continue
          if not (a.all or a.almost_all) and a.no_dotfiles and e.name.startswith('.'): continue
          ep=os.path.join(d,e.name); paths.append(ep)
          try: isdir=e.is_dir(follow_symlinks=False)
          except OSError: isdir=False
          if isdir and (a.recursive or a.tree) and level < max(1,a.depth if a.depth else 999999): walk(ep,level+1)
      walk(a.directory,1)
    rows=[]
    for path in paths:
      x=meta(path)
      if not x: continue
      typ=x['file_type']; n=x['name']
      if a.no_dotfiles and n.startswith('.'): continue
      if a.dotfiles_only and not n.startswith('.'): continue
      if a.dirs_only and typ!='dir' or a.files_only and typ!='file' or a.symlinks_only and typ!='symlink': continue
      if a.no_dirs and typ=='dir' or a.no_files and typ=='file' or a.no_symlinks and typ=='symlink': continue
      if a.filter and not filter_utils.name_matches(n,a.filter,a.case_sensitive): continue
      if a.size and not filter_utils.size_matches(x['size_bytes'],a.size): continue
      if a.modified:
        ts=datetime.fromisoformat(x['modified'].replace('Z','+00:00')).timestamp()
        if not filter_utils.time_matches(ts,a.modified): continue
      if a.created:
        ts=datetime.fromisoformat(x['created'].replace('Z','+00:00')).timestamp()
        if not filter_utils.time_matches(ts,a.created): continue
      if a.search and typ=='file':
        try:
          content=Path(path).read_text(errors='ignore'); pattern=a.search
          matched=(pattern[6:] in content if pattern.startswith('regex:') else pattern in content)
          if not matched: continue
        except Exception: continue
      rows.append(x)
    rows=sort_records(rows,criterion=a.sort,reverse=a.sort_reverse,dirs_first=a.sort_dirs_first,
                      case_sensitive=a.sort_case_sensitive,natural=a.sort_natural or a.sort=='name')
    if a.json:
      print(json.dumps(rows,indent=2 if a.pretty else None,ensure_ascii=False)); return 0
    if a.ndjson:
      for x in rows: print(json.dumps(x,separators=(',',':'),ensure_ascii=False))
      return 0
    if a.csv:
      print(csv_output(rows))
      return 0
    if a.long:
      for x in rows:
        try: mode=format_permissions(os.stat(x['path'],follow_symlinks=False).st_mode,a.permission_format)
        except Exception: mode=x['mode_octal']
        size=f"{x['size_bytes']:,}B"; suffix='/' if x['file_type']=='dir' else ('@' if x['file_type']=='symlink' else '')
        date=datetime.fromisoformat(x['modified'].replace('Z','+00:00')).strftime('%b %d %H:%M')
        g='' if a.hide_group else f" {x['owner_group']}"
        print(f"{mode} {size:>7} {date} {x['owner_user']}{g} {x['name']}{suffix}")
      return 0
    for x in rows: print(x['name']+('/' if x['file_type']=='dir' else ('@' if x['file_type']=='symlink' else '')))
    return 0
if __name__=='__main__':
    try: sys.exit(main())
    except BrokenPipeError: pass

"""CSV formatting compatible with lla's machine output."""

CSV_FIELDS = ("path", "name", "extension", "file_type", "size_bytes", "modified",
             "created", "accessed", "mode_octal", "owner_user", "owner_group",
             "inode", "hard_links", "symlink_target", "is_hidden", "git_status")


def csv_cell(value):
    """Render a field using lla's CSV quoting rules."""
    if value is None:
        return ""
    value = str(value)
    if any(ch in value for ch in ('"', ',', '\n', '\r')):
        return '"' + value.replace('"', '""') + '"'
    return value


def csv_output(rows):
    """Serialize metadata mappings with the stable v1 field ordering."""
    lines = [",".join(CSV_FIELDS)]
    lines.extend(",".join(csv_cell(row.get(field)) for field in CSV_FIELDS) for row in rows)
    return "\n".join(lines)

    a=parse_args(); root=os.path.abspath(a.directory)

    10      members=[]

    16                      if not name: continue
    17                      mode=(i.external_attr >> 16) & 0xffff
    18                      isdir=i.is_dir() or stat.S_ISDIR(mode)
    19                      if not mode: mode=0o755 if isdir else 0o600
    20                      ts=datetime(*i.date_time,tzinfo=timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')

"""Read-only metadata view for ZIP and tar archives."""
import os, stat, tarfile, zipfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import PurePosixPath

def archive_records(filename, recursive=False):
    low=filename.lower()
    if not low.endswith(('.zip','.tar','.tar.gz','.tgz')): return None
    source=os.path.abspath(filename)
    members=[]
    try:
        if zipfile.is_zipfile(filename):
            with zipfile.ZipFile(filename) as z:
                for i in z.infolist():
                    name=i.filename.rstrip('/')
                    if not name: continue
                    mode=(i.external_attr >> 16) & 0xffff
                    isdir=i.is_dir() or stat.S_ISDIR(mode)
                    if not mode: mode=0o755 if isdir else 0o600
                    # lla reports ZIP entries without a usable Unix timestamp as epoch.
                    ts='1970-01-01T00:00:00Z'
                    members.append((name,'dir' if isdir else 'file',0 if isdir else i.file_size,mode,ts))
        else:
            with tarfile.open(filename,'r:*') as t:
                for i in t.getmembers():
                    name=i.name.rstrip('/')
                    if not name: continue
                    typ='dir' if i.isdir() else ('symlink' if i.issym() else ('file' if i.isfile() else 'other'))
                    ts=datetime.fromtimestamp(i.mtime,timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')
                    members.append((name,typ,0 if typ=='dir' else i.size,i.mode,ts))
    except (OSError,tarfile.TarError,zipfile.BadZipFile): return None
    known={m[0]:m for m in members}; explicit_names=set(known); directories=set()
    for name,*_ in members:
        parts=PurePosixPath(name).parts
        for n in range(1,len(parts)):
            d='/'.join(parts[:n]); directories.add(d)
    for d in directories:
        if d not in known: known[d]=(d,'dir',0,0o755,'1970-01-01T00:00:00Z')
    selected=[]
    for name,item in known.items():
        if recursive or '/' not in name: selected.append(item)
    out=[]
    for name,typ,size,mode,modified in selected:
        basename=name.rsplit('/',1)[-1]
        ext=os.path.splitext(basename)[1][1:] or None
        out.append({'path':os.path.basename(filename)+'/'+name,'name':basename,'extension':ext,'file_type':typ,
          'size_bytes':size,'modified':modified,'created':None,'accessed':None,'mode_octal':f'{mode & 0o7777:04o}',
          'owner_user':'root','owner_group':'root','inode':None,'hard_links':None,'symlink_target':None,
          'is_hidden':basename.startswith('.'),'git_status':None,'plugin':({'archive_source':source} if name in explicit_names else {})})
    return out

content.text:
## Task and constraints

Reimplement `/opt/reference/executable` (`lla 0.5.7`) in Python 3.10 using only the standard library. Work in `/workspace`; run with `python3 main.py`. **Do not run `/workspace/compile.sh`.** Reference access is only through its normal CLI. Keep coordinating via the `group` tools and push all useful work to shared `team/main`.

## Progress

- Shared `main.py` now has broad CLI support, including listing formats, filters, config, search, plugins, themes, completion, diff, jump, and other subcommands.
- Integrated `archive_utils.py` for ZIP/TAR/TAR.GZ/TGZ virtual listings, including metadata, filters, JSON/CSV, long output, and tree output. Archive output was compared to reference fixtures; ZIP JSON and archive long/tree modes matched in the latest checks.
- Added/maintained installer command dispatch and metadata fixes, including filesystem birth timestamps via `statx`.
- Work is on shared `team/main`; the latest local `HEAD` had been fast-forwarded through `ee6176b` and a subsequent group update was observed as post #469. Fetch before editing or pushing.
- `python3 -m py_compile main.py archive_utils.py` and `python3 main.py --version` passed. Do not use `compile.sh`.

## Key behavioral findings

- Reference default JSON is compact and omits the final newline. Relative input paths stay relative; absolute input paths stay absolute.
- Tree/recursive JSON includes a root record and depth-first entries; hidden entries are omitted by default. With gitignore respect, root can be omitted.
- Symlink JSON puts target in `symlink_target` and `plugin.symlink_target`.
- ZIP member JSON reports epoch timestamps; TAR keeps member mtimes. Archive `--tree --json` expands contents without a virtual root; long archive listing expands nested entries.
- Reference symbolic long permissions have an unusual repeated symbolic rendering. Teammates verified the corresponding helper/output against reference fixtures.

## Current situation / next steps

1. Read the latest group feed and fetch/merge `team/main` before making changes.
2. Continue broad parity review on the latest main; do not duplicate teammate work. Recent open findings include sizemap bar sizing/width and timeline calendar-day boundaries (posts #459 and #461).
3. Run focused reference comparisons for any concrete mismatch, patch the shared implementation, merge latest `team/main`, and push fast-forward.
4. Check `git status` and `git log` before finalizing. The user expects sustained work until time runs out, not an early stop.
I’ll check the latest team branch and group updates first, then compare the current implementation against the reference for the open sizemap and timeline issues.

def recursive_file_bytes(directory):
    total=0
